[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Marion Glasgow''' was baptised at Edinburgh on 29 January 1657, a daughter of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow (1626-)]], weaver, and '''[[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]]'''.<ref name="MarionBaptism">“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', Marione Glesgow, baptised 29 January 1657, Edinburgh, daughter of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YD-PR2 record X1YD-PR2].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Marion married '''William Calder''' at Edinburgh on 29 June 1686.<ref name="MarionMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Marion; William Calder 29 June 1686.”</ref>

On 30 June 1686, the day after their marriage, William was admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh. The entry describes him as a weaver and states that his admission was by right of his wife Marion, daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess.<ref name="CalderBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 91: “Calder, Wm., B., weaver, be r. of w. Marion, dr. to James Glasgow, weaver, B. 30 June 1686.”</ref>

This entry directly establishes both Marion's marriage to William Calder and her relationship to her father.

Marion's date and place of death have not been identified.

== Research Notes ==
=== Parentage ===

Marion's baptism names James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan as her parents.<ref name="MarionBaptism" />

William Calder's burgess admission independently identifies Marion as a daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh.<ref name="CalderBurgess" />

The father named in these records was the Edinburgh weaver apprenticed in 1641 and admitted as a burgess in 1649. He was distinct from the James Glasgow baptised at Inveresk in 1626 as a son of Alexander Glasgow.

=== Name and date ===

The baptismal index records her name as “Marione Glesgow.” The later marriage and burgess records use the form Marion Glasgow.

The baptism dated 29 January 1657 is Marion's record. It is not evidence for a son named James Glasgow born on that date.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original 1657 baptism entry;
* William Calder's apprenticeship and incorporation records;
* baptismal records for any children of Marion and William;
* property or burgess records concerning the Calder household;
* testaments for Marion, William or their parents; and
* burial records for Marion and William.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Marion Glasgow and John Gray on 30 September 1686 at Carriden.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 664/10 / 109; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marione Glasgow with John Rait, tailor, on 28 June 1659.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 48; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 560; PDF pp.277 and 570; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=570 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Marion Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Marion Glasgow with John Bruce, smith, on 4 July 1684.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 251; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 96; PDF pp.277 and 106; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=106 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.
